Yes. The matching paper is Fast and Geometrically Grounded Lorentz Neural Networks by Robert van der Klis and coauthors [1]. It studies hyperbolic neural networks in the Lorentz model and argues that existing Lorentz linear layers make output hyperbolic norms grow only logarithmically with gradient descent steps, undermining hyperbolic geometry’s advantage [1].

The paper proposes a new Lorentz linear layer based on a distance-to-hyperplane formulation, and proves this restores the usual linear scaling of output hyperbolic norms with gradient descent steps [1]. It also adds Lorentzian activation functions and a caching strategy, aiming for networks that better respect hyperbolic geometry while narrowing the computation gap to Euclidean neural networks [1].
